title: [bug] flows:list/get/export are unauthenticated reads
description:

title: Ambiguous host timeout: reconcile a mutation that may or may not have been applied
description:
Carved out of awkit-9yv, which was closed on the rest of its criteria.

A request that exceeds its deadline is AMBIGUOUS: the host may have applied it, may
be about to, or may have died before touching the collection. ZvecUtilityHostManager
enforces deadlines and verify:zvec-host-lifecycle asserts the deadline VALUES are
sane (close/shutdown inside the 2s quit budget, query < open), but nothing verifies
what the system concludes about the mutation itself.

The queue must not blind-replay an ambiguous write, and must not silently drop it
either. Upserts are idempotent by deterministic id so a replay is safe; deletes are
idempotent too; deleteByEntity is idempotent. The risk is the COUNT and the
rebuildRequired decision, not the data - a timeout currently classifies through
SemanticMutationQueue retry classification, and it is untested whether that
classification is correct for an ambiguous outcome as opposed to a clean failure.

Needed:
- decide and document the policy for an ambiguous timeout (retry vs mark
  rebuild-required vs surface degraded);
- exercise it through the REAL utility host, where a timeout can actually race a
  write, not against a fake that resolves deterministically;
- add the case to verify:semantic-rebuild-live, which already kills the host
  mid-write and mid-populate and is the natural home for it.

Note for whoever picks this up: verify:zvec-host-lifecycle Timeout
notes: Policy implemented: SEMANTIC_HOST_TIMEOUT and SEMANTIC_HOST_EXITED during a dispatched write map to AMBIGUOUS_MUTATION. The queue never retries that class, abandons it, and marks rebuildRequired so authoritative source rebuild reconciles whether the host applied the operation or not. Verified through the real utility host with a 1,500-document zero-deadline write: one dispatch, one abandonment, rebuild required, no requeue. verify:semantic-store 153/153; verify:semantic-rebuild-live 24/24 with 68 assertions; semantic queue 70/70; build and script typecheck pass. Mutation disabled the mapping and produced 152/153 with three write attempts, then reverted.
close_reason: Ambiguous mutation outcomes are never blind-replayed and require authoritative rebuild, proven through the real host.

title: Semantic rebuild orchestration and generation activation
description: Keep the active generation queryable; build the candidate through the serialized rebuild path; populate only validated documents; validate schema + exact count + per-kind counts + sourceHash samples + query samples; close the candidate BEFORE pointer activation; the pointer swap is the commit point; retain one rollback generation; clear the queue and rebuildRequired flag only after successful activation; a failed candidate must never change the active pointer.
notes:
2026-07-25 (commit 67835cd, hardened by 002e684): IMPLEMENTED and verified against in-memory stores plus a generation-lifecycle stub - verify:semantic-rebuild 61/0. SemanticRebuildOrchestrator + queue watermark and ordered delta journal. Every listed requirement holds EXCEPT one, which was deliberately superseded: 'clear the queue after successful activation' is UNSAFE and is not done. A candidate is built from a snapshot, so the queue can hold mutations that postdate it; clearing on activation silently discards the user's most recent changes. Those mutations are journalled and replayed into the candidate before activation instead, and anything accepted during the replay stays pending and drains against the new generation. Delta completeness is judged against the CAPTURED entry set, not the live journal - judging against the live journal failed any rebuild that overlapped a write, so a busy index could never finish one. Journal overflow refuses activation rather than dropping entries. whenIdle() is now bounded by wall-clock as well as iterations (an iteration bound does not bound time; a wedged rebuild would have held shutdown open forever). NOT DONE: the orchestrator is not bound to a real generation root - rebuildGeneration/openCandidate/retarget still need wiring to rebuildIntoNewGeneration and a real runtime root, and whenIdle() has no production shutdown caller. This is the last structural gap in Phase 1B.
2026-07-28 CLOSED. The two "NOT DONE" items in the 2026-07-25 note were already stale:
SemanticIndexRuntime imports rebuildIntoNewGeneration and injects rebuildGeneration/openCandidate/
retarget into the orchestrator, and whenIdle() has had a production shutdown caller via
SemanticIndexRuntime.shutdown() <- disposeSemanticSubsystem().

The gap the note did NOT name was the real one: SemanticIndexRuntime was never constructed or
registered in the Electron main process. setSemanticIndexRuntime had ZERO callers and
new SemanticIndexRuntime appeared only in scripts/zvec-harness/harnessMain.ts. Consequences, all
fail-open: semanticHealth() derived rebuildRequired and activeGenerationOpenFailed from a null
runtime and so reported healthy unconditionally; disposeSemanticSubsystem left drained=true because
there was nothing to drain, recording EVERY session as a clean shutdown; and rebuild() had no
production entry point at all.

Fixed by: app/main/semantic/semanticSnapshot.ts (authoritative flow+workflow snapshot over the
existing projectAndValidate pipeline; sources injected so a tsx verifier can drive it without
Electron; an unreadable store THROWS rather than returning a partial snapshot, which the
orchestrator turns into SNAPSHOT_FAILED with nothing allocated); registration in
getSemanticHostManager() with the host manager itself as the ZvecHostTransport; and
initializeSemanticSubsystem() now calling the registrar after reconciliation. Constructors are inert,
so plan 16.1 holds -- startup still spawns no host. Added ensureSemanticIndexOpen() and
rebuildSemanticIndex() as the production open/rebuild entry points. Snapshot sources are resolved
PER REBUILD, not captured at startup, because the flow/workflow folders are user-configurable.

Proof: verify:semantic-store 179/0 (was 153), verify:semantic-rebuild 64/0, verify:semantic-queue
70/0, real-host verify:semantic-rebuild-live 24/0 with 68 assertions, build PASS,
verify:verifier-classification reconciled. Four mutations were run and all went red before revert:
leaking a step value into stepNames (privacy), deleting the registration, degrading an unreadable
source to a partial snapshot, and removing the startup registrar call. The registration guard FAILED
its own first mutation -- counting setSemanticIndexRuntime( call sites was satisfied by the
degrade path's setSemanticIndexRuntime(null) -- and was rewritten to assert the constructed runtime
is the one registered.

NOT covered: no product surface calls ensureSemanticIndexOpen()/rebuildSemanticIndex() yet, because
there is still no semantic IPC/preload/UI. That is the next phase (service -> RBAC -> preload ->
projections -> UI), not this bead. Production registration is proven by source-scan guards plus the
real-host lifecycle suite, not by a real-Electron end-to-end run.

title: Zvec host: add scan/count/cursor + typed filters to remove the 100-document ceiling
description: The utility host protocol has no scan or cursor operation. Its query is top-K capped at 100 and the raw host returns hit counts plus ten ids, not documents. Consequently ZvecSemanticStore cannot implement deleteByEntity, stats, clear or an exact totalMatched correctly, and currently declares capabilities.entityOperations=false and throws UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION for them (safer than silently truncating). Search also over-fetches the global top 100 then applies AWKIT filters after ranking, so a filtered match ranked outside the unfiltered top 100 is never returned and totalMatched is not the true filtered total. Needs: typed host operations (scan with cursor/page, exact count, deleteByEntity, clearCollection, query with typed filters applied INSIDE the trusted adapter/host, never a raw filter expression crossing SemanticStore). Proofs required: clear 1500 docs leaves zero; delete an entity with >100 docs leaves zero; a filtered match beyond the unfiltered top 100 is found; totalMatched exact.
notes: RESOLVED in code on main (f4f6a37, 5f6250a). Host protocol v2 adds typed scan/count/deleteByFilter; ZvecSemanticStore.capabilities.entityOperations is now true. All four required proofs hold against the REAL @zvec/zvec binding via verify:semantic-zvec-filter (63/0): clear removes all 1501 docs; an entity with 130 docs (>100) deletes completely; a filtered match ranked last of 1501 is found at topk=10 while the unfiltered top-10 excludes it (negative-controlled); totalMatched is exact via a count-only second pass. The original premise was WRONG: the 100-doc ceiling was AWKIT's own Math.min(topK,100) in the host, not a vendor limit, and deleteByFilterSync existed all along. Filters cross IPC as typed clauses only; the host builds the expression from an allowlist (duplicated deliberately, drift-checked). Value rule is a REFUSAL not an escaper - measured: escaping only quotes throws on backslash values, escaping both silently matches NOTHING. RESIDUAL GAP: the host's own code path (its duplicated builder, two-pass query, post-delete re-scan) is asserted by source-drift checks, not executed through a real utilityProcess. That execution proof is awkit-9yv.
close_reason: Implemented on main (f4f6a37, 5f6250a); all four required proofs verified against the real binding. Remaining end-to-end proof through a real utilityProcess is tracked by awkit-9yv, which already specifies exactly that.

title: Damaged active-generation pointer is read as absent, allowing reconciliation to delete every generation
description: readActivePointer() returns null for missing, unreadable, malformed-JSON, and invalid-name pointer states alike. semanticService passes that null as authoritativeActiveGeneration, which skips the 'preserve everything' early-return and the per-generation protection check in reconcileGenerations; with metadata reporting an unclean shutdown (its default on any read failure) every generation is then rm -rf'd, including the live one. Same defect class as 4ddc773, relocated to the pointer reader. Fix: readActivePointerStrict with ok/missing/invalid/unreadable, validate all three pointer fields, and make invalid/unreadable mean 'active identity unknown' => preserve all, no cleanup, report ACTIVE_POINTER_READ_FAILED, require recovery/rebuild, keep startup non-blocking.

title: Make offline packaging inputs versioned and verifiable
description:
Packaged artifacts are NOT reproducible from source control, and a clean checkout can produce a
valid-LOOKING but unusable application.

Found while regenerating artifacts from 61f6099 (see C:\Users\moham\awkit-build-evidence\61f6099\provenance.md).

Problems:
1. `vendor/` is fully gitignored (0 files tracked). `resources/browsers/` and
   `resources/oracle-jdbc/` are gitignored too -- only 27 of 339 `resources/` files are tracked.
   electron-builder.json copies BOTH trees wholesale as `extraResources`.
   => A pristine checkout builds a ~830 MB-lighter artifact with NO bundled Chromium. It packages
      and launches, but cannot automate anything. Nothing fails loudly.
2. `scripts/prepare-offline-deps.ps1:17` runs a bare, unqualified `npx playwright install chromium`
   and copies whatever lands in the machine's ms-playwright cache. No version is requested, pinned,
   or verified before the copy.
3. CLEAN_MACHINE_VALIDATION_RUNBOOK.md §2 pins the final artifact SHA-256 but NOT the browser
   payload that materially determines the artifact's behaviour and most of its bytes.
   => The hash pins roughly half the input.
4. `resources/dependency-manifest.json`.`application.builtAt` records MANIFEST REGENERATION time,
   not the age of the bundled browser payload. Observed concretely: a 2026-07-22 build wrote
   builtAt=2026-07-22 while shipping the Chromium payload dated 2026-07-10. A reader would date the
   payload 12 days later than it is. (Split out as its own P2 bead -- see the metadata-naming bead.)
acceptance_criteria:
1. Packaging FAILS FAST, before the build, when required offline resources are missing or
   incomplete -- never produces a hollow artifact.
2. Expected Chromium and Playwright versions are explicit and declared in-repo.
3. The installed browser payload is verified by version AND hash before it is copied into
   vendor/ / resources/browsers/.
4. No bare, floating browser installation. `npx playwright install chromium` is replaced by a
   version-qualified, verified acquisition step.
5. Artifact provenance records, together: source commit, browser version, browser-payload
   hash + source date, Playwright version, Electron version, final artifact hash.
6. A clean checkout + an approved offline payload produces a COMPLETE package with no network
   access.
7. Reproducibility is validated by SEMANTIC PAYLOAD EQUIVALENCE, not whole-artifact hash equality:
   compare decompressed payload paths, sizes, and per-entry CRCs between the two artifacts,
   EXCLUDING known volatile generated metadata (currently
   `resources\resources\dependency-manifest.json` and its `vendor\` copy). Any other differing
   entry is real drift and must be investigated.
8. Whole-installer SHA-256 equality is NOT expected while build-time timestamps are embedded.
   `scripts/package-per-user-installer.ps1` regenerates `resources/dependency-manifest.json` (fresh
   `builtAt`) on every run and packages it, so two builds from byte-identical inputs yield
   different installer hashes. Final artifact SHA-256 is still recorded for runbook pinning and
   integrity verification -- it identifies the SPECIFIC ACCEPTED BUILD and must not be presented as
   proof of reproducible compilation. See awkit-c0c for the metadata split that would reduce this.
notes:
P1 because the failure mode is silent: a clean checkout yields a package that installs and launches but cannot drive a browser. Evidence + logs: C:\Users\moham\awkit-build-evidence\61f6099\. Keep SEPARATE from the clean-machine acceptance gate and from the 61f6099 artifact regeneration -- this is a repository-quality defect, not a release blocker for the current gate.
2026-07-28 Codex: implemented the authorized fail-loud half only. Both portable and NSIS packaging wrappers now invoke validate-offline-bundle.ps1 -PackagingInputsOnly before npm run build. The preflight names the exact resources/browsers/chromium/chrome.exe path and refuses missing or zero-byte inputs. Positive gate passed on the current payload; missing-file and empty-file mutations both failed loudly. Full validate:offline and strict validation pass. Bead remains OPEN because acceptance items 2-8 and the Chromium vendoring/reproducibility strategy require the owner decision explicitly reserved by docs/ai/tasks/DASHBOARD_BACKLOG_PROGRAM.md.
close_reason: Closed with exact Playwright/CfT pins and archive/tree/executable hashes, Ed25519-signed manifest plus startup verification, fail-fast packaging gates, artifact provenance, tamper tests, deterministic Oracle bridge, and clean-clone offline packaging. Two independent portable artifacts matched across 571 decompressed entries after excluding the generated signed manifest metadata and normalizing only Zvec builtAt.

title: Artifact profile screenshotOnFailure is computed but never read
description:
Configuration-contract defect: the Flow Designer and the resolved artifact profile imply one
behaviour while the runtime follows a different switch.

`resolveArtifactSettings()` returns `screenshotOnFailure` for all four profiles
(src/runner/artifacts/ArtifactProfile.ts:22-38), but NOTHING READS IT. The real gate is
`step.onFailure?.screenshot ?? true` (src/runner/FlowExecutor.ts:446).

Result: the `production` artifact profile does not actually control failure screenshots, and
`AWKIT_ARTIFACT_PROFILE=production` does not lean out failure-screenshot capture as documented.
Config that lies.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An explicit precedence contract is implemented and documented:

     explicit per-step override    (step.onFailure.screenshot, when present)
       -> artifact profile default (resolveArtifactSettings().screenshotOnFailure)
         -> safe system default    (capture)

   Concretely: the `?? true` fallback becomes `?? resolvedArtifactSettings.screenshotOnFailure`.
2. Flows that EXPLICITLY disable failure screenshots continue to disable them. The profile governs
   only steps with NO explicit override.
3. AWKIT_ARTIFACT_PROFILE=production demonstrably suppresses failure screenshots for steps with no
   explicit override; balanced/debug/full still capture.
4. Regression test proves the old always-capture behaviour is gone for the profile-governed case
   AND that the explicit opt-out still wins.
5. Either the field is wired (preferred) or removed -- no third state where it exists unread.
notes: Spec: docs/SRS_BROWSER_AUTOMATION_OBSERVABILITY.md FR-A4 change-dependency (Tranche 0). Prerequisite for detail-tiered observability: do not ship a second tier on top of a tier that already lies about one of its three fields. Keep SEPARATE from the evidence-ordering bead (awkit-oyc) despite adjacent code.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 159366b (screenshotOnFailure precedence now read); merged to main via PR #27 (merge 43255f1).

title: Failure evidence is captured after the retry loop, not at the failing attempt
description:
The failure screenshot is taken in `FlowExecutor.runStepWithRetries` AFTER the whole retry loop
finishes (src/runner/FlowExecutor.ts:446-448), guarded by `step.onFailure?.screenshot ?? true`.

Consequences:
- Retries that navigate, refresh, dismiss a dialog, or re-render DESTROY the broken state before it
  is photographed. The captured image is not the failure.
- Intermediate failed attempts get no evidence at all.

`StepExecutor.execute`'s catch block (src/runner/StepExecutor.ts:287-307) already holds the correct
per-attempt scope and already saves the trace chunk there for exactly this reason -- evidence
capture belongs alongside it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Evidence is captured INSIDE the failing attempt's scope, before any retry, recovery, or
   navigation can alter page state.
2. Each retry attempt produces its own evidence set; attempt n's evidence is never overwritten by
   attempt n+1.
3. Each failed attempt preserves all four independently:
     - original exception  (always primary; never replaced)
     - attempt-specific evidence  (screenshot, DOM, a11y, console tail, network state)
     - trace chunk  (existing TraceService.endStep behaviour)
     - retry decision  (the RetryPolicy verdict + reason; runtime_node_attempts.retryDecision)
4. Evidence-capture failure is APPENDED as a secondary diagnostic and never replaces, masks, or
   reorders the original automation error. A dead page still reports the step's real failure.
5. Evidence filenames encode runId, flowId, stepId, pageId, attemptId, timestamp.
6. Capture is bounded -- a hung page must not block the failure path indefinitely.
7. `StepExecutionResult.screenshotPath` STILL populated with the last capture (FlowExecutor.ts:446
   checks `!lastResult.screenshotPath` and the reports UI reads it). New per-attempt refs are
   additive.
8. Captures routed through the existing OperationLimiters (`limitOp`) so concurrent runs do not
   stampede on screenshots.
notes: Spec: docs/SRS_BROWSER_AUTOMATION_OBSERVABILITY.md FR-B2 (Tranche 1). Highest diagnostic value per unit of risk; independent of CDP. Preserve the step.onFailure.screenshot opt-out -- saved flows rely on it. Keep as a SEPARATE bead from the artifact-profile precedence fix (awkit-5yx) even though the code is adjacent: different failure mode, different acceptance criteria, different rollback boundary.
close_reason: Reconciled the shipped FR-B2 fix from 269cd70/b4d2974: FlowExecutor captures every failing attempt before RetryPolicy.decide, accumulates evidence without replacing the automation error, and preserves screenshotPath. Extended verify:failure-evidence with an explicit capture-before-decision timeline sentinel: 35/35; moving decide ahead of capture produced 34/35 and was reverted. Real Chromium evidence output remains 17/17.

title: Popup registration is non-deterministic: one Page registered under two aliases
description:
A single popup Page is registered under TWO aliases by two independent call sites.

- `PlaywrightRunner.runFlowWithChildren` installs a context-level `page` handler that assigns

title: Designer round trip silently drops a bare FlowStep.value (condition expressions)
description:
DATA LOSS. fromFlowStep (app/renderer/components/workflow/flowStepMapping.ts) derives the node's value as:

    step.url ?? valueSource?.value ?? valueSource?.key ?? valueSource?.envKey ?? valueSource?.path ?? valueSource?.outputKey ?? ""

It NEVER reads step.value. So a FlowStep carrying only `value` (no `valueSource`, and not a goto) resolves to "" on load, and toFlowStep then emits `value: data.value || undefined` -> undefined. The value is destroyed by one designer open+save, with no error shown.

REACHABLE ON SHIPPED DATA: resources/test-fixtures/mock-site/flows/mock-conditional-flow.json stores its condition node with a `value` expression and no valueSource. Confirmed against the real converters:

    BEFORE  value = "<runtimeInputs.path expression>"   valueSource = undefined
    AFTER   value = undefined                           valueSource = undefined
    RESULT: condition expression LOST

Impact: opening such a flow in the Flow Designer and saving turns a working conditional into an empty one. A scan of resources/** found 69 steps with 1 currently affected. Externally authored or imported flows can hit this more broadly, since FlowStep.value is an independent optional field in the schema.

Found by scripts/verify-flow-step-mapping.mts during the Serialization Round-Trip Hardening phase. NOT introduced by the extraction: the moved functions are byte-identical to the originals (proven by diff). Pre-existing defect.

Current behavior is PINNED by two checks in that verifier under the "KNOWN DEFECT" section. When this is fixed, those two checks must be inverted.

Likely fix: either have fromFlowStep fall back to step.value when there is no url and no valueSource, OR require producers to always emit a static valueSource alongside value. Both are runtime behavior changes, so both were deliberately excluded from the hardening phase. Needs a decision on which side owns the invariant.

title: RT-14: value and valueSource flattened through one designer string, corrupting typed sources
description:
fromFlowStep collapses FlowStep.value and FlowStep.valueSource into a single data.value via: step.url ?? valueSource?.value ?? valueSource?.key ?? valueSource?.envKey ?? valueSource?.path ?? valueSource?.outputKey ?? "". createValueSource then rebuilds a typed source from that one string.

Most damaging round-trip finding. On a goto, step.url is FIRST in the chain and shadows the source entirely: {type:env, envKey:AWKIT_LAB_ENV_ALPHA} returns as {type:env, envKey:http://127.0.0.1:4321/form.html}, and {type:generated, generator:randomEmail} returns with a generator value outside its own union (a structurally invalid document). For other types, FlowStep.value is overwritten with the SOURCE KEY, destroying the literal fallback the runner would use. Sources whose discriminating field is not in the chain (secret, dynamic) collapse to empty and are dropped - this is also the mechanism behind RT-02.

Owner: app/renderer/components/workflow/flowProfileMapping.ts (fromFlowStep + createValueSource).
Fix: model the value source structurally in FlowDesignerNodeData instead of flattening. Immediate containment: remove step.url from the head of the recovery chain - it is the only entry that can silently overwrite an unrelated source field.

title: Oracle soak: Node peak RSS grows ~5x across a 30-min run (2472MB peak) with no check covering it
description:
SEPARATE from awkit-cww, which was about the leak STATISTIC and is now fixed. This is a distinct failure mode that no invariant currently guards.

Clean idle-host 30-min soak 2026-07-26 (commit dce4204), 18,243,386 queries at 9,746/s, failures=0:

  node RSS series (28 samples, MB):
  137 142 294 199 154 188 499 152 358 | 287 160 281 561 593 849 1289 505 696 | 191 507 954 434 1859 2472 245 1295 1887 1356

  floor (min 1st third -> min last third): 137 -> 245 MB (+108, PASSES the 150MB gate at 72% of budget)
  slope: +52.14 MB/sample = +1460 MB across the run
  endpointDelta: +1219 MB
  peak: 2472 MB

NOT A LEAK: the last third still returns to 245MB, close to the 137MB start, so the process demonstrably still reclaims memory. The floor gate is correct to pass.

THE ACTUAL CONCERN: peak amplitude grows roughly 5x (first third maxes at 499MB; last third hits 1859, 2472, 1887). A 2.4GB transient peak is an OOM risk on a constrained machine and nothing currently fails on it. The floor statistic is the right leak detector but is blind to this by construction.

ALSO: this refutes the concurrent-load confound hypothesis recorded on awkit-cww. The IDLE run is WORSE than the confounded one on every peak-sensitive statistic - slope +1460 vs +1106, endpoint +1219 vs +651, peak 2472 vs 1872. The behaviour is intrinsic, not an artifact of sharing the machine with packaging and GUI verifiers.

SUGGESTED: decide whether a peak-RSS ceiling belongs in the soak invariants, and derive it from a measured baseline rather than from this run. Investigate what allocates so heavily late in a run at ~10k queries/s - one connection is opened and closed per query, so per-query allocation churn is the obvious place to look. The full series is now recorded in reports/oracle-validation/oracle-soak.json (memory.nodeRssSeriesMb) so this can be re-analysed without another 30-minute run.
notes:
2026-07-26 INVESTIGATED. Two root causes, neither of them a product leak. The second one invalidates the SIGNAL both the old and the new check are built on.

CAUSE 1 - THE HARNESS MEASURES ITSELF.
benchmark-oracle-jdbc.mts:185 pushes one element into 'latencies' PER QUERY, unbounded, and :186 does the same for 'dbTimes'. At the clean run's 18,243,386 queries that array alone is 502 MB of LIVE data (measured: survives a forced GC unchanged), against a 30 MB baseline. dbTimes stayed empty in mock mode - the artifact shows dbTimeMs p50=p95=0 - so a LIVE run would roughly double this. The end-of-run [...arr].sort() copies add ~30 MB more. So most of the 'growth' this bead was filed about is the benchmark accumulating its own samples, growing linearly with throughput x duration. It is not the product.

CAUSE 2 - RSS IS NOT A VALID LEAK SIGNAL ON WINDOWS. This is the important one.
process.memoryUsage().rss is the WORKING SET, which the OS trims independently of the process. Measured directly: with an 18.2M-element array live, rss=499MB heapTotal=503MB heapUsed=470MB; after a SetProcessWorkingSetSize trim, rss=5MB while heapUsed stayed 470MB and the array was still fully live. RSS fell 99% with ZERO change in live heap.

That explains the implausible soak samples - 2472MB -> 245MB in 60 seconds is the OS trimming, not the process releasing - and it reconciles the arithmetic that did not previously add up: the last-third floor read 245MB while the latencies array alone had to be ~400-500MB live at that point.

CONSEQUENCE FOR awkit-cww (CLOSED): floor-rise is a genuinely better STATISTIC than the endpoint delta and the negative controls stand, but it is computed over a signal the OS manipulates. A trim landing inside the first window inflates the measured rise; one landing in the last window masks it. The fix was an improvement, not a sound gate, and closing awkit-cww overstated it.

RECOMMENDED, in order:
1. Stop accumulating per-query samples. Use fixed-bucket histograms (1ms buckets to some ceiling + overflow) for the latency/dbTime percentiles - O(1) memory, exact enough for p50/p95/p99, and removes ~500MB of self-inflicted growth. Keep the existing pct() semantics.
2. Gate on heapUsed, not rss. V8's own accounting is immune to working-set trimming (measured above: unchanged across a trim that moved RSS by 494MB). Keep rssTrend() and apply it to the heapUsed series; keep RSS as a DIAGNOSTIC only.
3. Only then decide whether a peak ceiling is still needed - with 1 and 2 done, the remaining signal is finally about the product.

Do NOT simply raise a threshold; the numbers being compared are not the process's memory.
close_reason:
RESOLVED in c6d4547 — and the answer is that there was never a product leak. The growth was the harness measuring itself.

Full 30-minute soak with the fixed harness: 9 PASS / 0 FAIL. 23,458,521 queries at 13,030/s, failures=0, cancellation ok=59 bad=0 p95 252ms, clean teardown.

  node HEAP floor 11 -> 8 MB (rise -3MB), slope +0.08MB/sample (+2MB over the run), peak 24MB
  node RSS  floor 78 -> 78 MB (rise 0), slope 0, peak 80MB
  bridge RSS floor 194 -> 193 MB (-1)

  heap series: 14 11 11 18 14 14 21 20 16 13 12 17 24 16 15 21 13 16 21 13 16 20 20 20 8 18 18 12 19
  rss series : 78 79 79 80 80 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 79 78 78 79 79 79 78 79 79 79 79

Heap oscillates in a tight 8-24MB band with no trend; RSS is flat at 78-80MB for thirty minutes.

Same workload, before vs after the harness fix:
  peak RSS      2472MB -> 80MB
  throughput    9,746/s -> 13,030/s (+34%)
  max latency   36,727ms -> 4,681ms

The +34% throughput and the collapse in max latency are the tell: the harness was spending roughly a third of the machine on its own accounting, and the multi-second latency outliers were GC pauses from the per-minute [...latencies].sort() over an array holding one entry per query.

NUANCE worth recording rather than overstating: with the harness fixed, RSS is stable enough that it would have carried the verdict fine. The Windows working-set finding (rss can fall 99% with heapUsed unchanged) is real and measured, and moving the verdict to heapUsed is still correct because a trim CAN corrupt an RSS verdict while heap cannot be trimmed - but cause 1 (the harness) was the dominant one. Cause 2 is why the numbers never reconciled, not why the gate broke.

No peak-RSS ceiling is being added: with the harness fixed there is nothing left to ceiling. Revisit only if a future run shows peak growth against a flat heap.

title: benchmark:oracle-jdbc Node RSS leak check fails; endpoint-delta method cannot distinguish a leak from GC sawtooth
description:
RED GATE, reported truthfully - do NOT loosen the threshold to make it pass.

Run 2026-07-26 at 94c858e: 8 passed, 1 failed. Failing check: 'Node (Specter) RSS did not leak (drift < 150MB)' - drift=651MB over 28 samples (start 104MB, end 755MB). Everything else passed: full 30.2 min, 19,659,232 queries at 10,864.8/s, failures=0, cancellation ok=56 bad=0 p95=251ms, bridge (Java) RSS drift -37MB, pending=0, no orphan Java, no pool metrics.

METHOD WEAKNESS: scripts/benchmark-oracle-jdbc.mts:246 computes rssDrift = nodeRss[last] - nodeRss[0], a two-point endpoint delta, then line 288 compares abs() against 150. It ignores the other 26 samples. The observed series is a strong sawtooth: 104 126 159 319 138 363 521 328 328 53 ... 745 1286 827 1872 755. It DIPS TO 53MB at t+10.3m, BELOW the 104MB start - a monotonic leak cannot decrease, so the process demonstrably returns memory. But the peaks do rise (521 -> 745 -> 1286 -> 1872), so growth in the high-water mark is NOT ruled out. The endpoint delta would have 'passed' had the final sample landed in a trough, so the check is close to arbitrary on this signal.

CONFOUND: this run shared the machine with electron-builder packaging, Electron GUI verifiers and Chromium workloads. Re-run on an otherwise-idle host before drawing conclusions.

SUGGESTED FIX (owner decision - changing the method while the gate is red risks moving the goalposts): replace the endpoint delta with a trend statistic (least-squares slope over all samples, or median of the first quartile vs the last quartile), derive the threshold from a MEASURED idle-host baseline, and record how it was measured so the next person raises it rather than lowering it to match a failure. Consider also recording the high-water mark separately from the trend.

NOT caused by this session's changes (manualApproval routing, packaging staleness guard, validate-offline output, mock-site fixture) - none touch Oracle JDBC or memory. The artifact reports/oracle-validation/oracle-soak.json is untracked, so there is no committed baseline to diff against.
notes:
2026-07-26 FOLLOW-UP — closing this was premature in one respect. See awkit-q0e.

The floor-rise statistic is a real improvement over the endpoint delta and its 10 negative controls stand. But it is computed over process.memoryUsage().rss, and RSS on Windows is the WORKING SET, which the OS trims independently of the process. Measured: an 18.2M-element array live gave rss=499MB / heapUsed=470MB; after a SetProcessWorkingSetSize trim, rss=5MB while heapUsed was UNCHANGED at 470MB and the array was still fully live.

So a trim landing inside the first sampling window inflates the measured floor rise, and one landing in the last window masks it. The gate is better than what it replaced but is not yet sound. The remedy (gate on heapUsed, keep RSS as a diagnostic) is tracked on awkit-q0e together with the harness's unbounded per-query sample arrays, which contribute ~502MB of the observed growth by themselves.

Leaving this CLOSED because the statistic change it describes is done and committed in dce4204; the signal change is a separate piece of work.
close_reason:
Fixed in dce4204. The check now gates on FLOOR RISE (min last third - min first third) with the original 150MB/200MB budgets unchanged - a change of statistic, not a relaxation. Verified on a clean idle-host 30-min soak: 9 PASS / 0 FAIL. Node floor 137->245MB (+108, 72% of budget); bridge floor 157->156MB (-1). Negative-controlled 10/10 before the run.

Two corrections recorded for the next reader: (1) the trend statistics made the ORIGINAL failure MORE credible, not less - my earlier 'endpoint delta is close to arbitrary' framing was wrong in the exonerating direction; (2) the concurrent-load confound hypothesis is REFUTED - the idle run is worse than the confounded one on slope (+1460 vs +1106), endpoint (+1219 vs +651) and peak (2472 vs 1872).

The gate is green because the statistic now measures the right thing, NOT because memory behaviour improved. Peak-RSS growth is real, uncovered by any check, and split out as awkit-q0e.

title: dependency-manifest builtAt conflates manifest regeneration with payload provenance
description:
`resources/dependency-manifest.json` has a single `application.builtAt` field that records when the
MANIFEST was regenerated -- but readers naturally interpret it as the vintage of the bundled
runtime payload it describes.

Observed concretely during the 61f6099 artifact regeneration (2026-07-22):
  application.builtAt = 2026-07-22T20:47:18Z   <- manifest regeneration (this build)
  browsers[0].version = 149.0.7827.55          <- payload actually dated 2026-07-10

`generate-dependency-manifest.ps1` rewrites the file on every `package:portable` run, so builtAt
tracks the build, never the payload. Anyone auditing provenance from this manifest would date the
Chromium payload 12 days later than it is.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Manifest metadata distinguishes manifest generation from payload provenance, with explicit
   separate fields, e.g.:
     manifestGeneratedAt     - when THIS manifest was written
     browserPayloadBuiltAt   - when the browser payload was produced / obtained
     browserPayloadSource    - how it was obtained, including the version requested
     browserPayloadHash      - hash of the copied payload
2. `builtAt` must NOT imply the age of Chromium or of any other copied dependency. Either rename
   it, or restrict its documented meaning to manifest generation alone.
3. Existing readers of `builtAt` keep working, or are updated in the same change.
4. The distinction is documented wherever artifact provenance is recorded.
5. Payload provenance fields are what artifact comparison and runbook pinning rely on -- see
   awkit-epz criteria 7-8: while a build-time timestamp remains embedded in a packaged file,
   whole-artifact hash equality cannot be used as reproducibility evidence.
notes: Split out of awkit-epz so that bead stays focused on reproducibility. This one is metadata naming/semantics only -- smaller scope, no packaging behaviour change. Evidence: C:\Users\moham\awkit-build-evidence\61f6099\provenance.md
close_reason: Manifest schema v2 replaces ambiguous application.builtAt with top-level manifestGeneratedAt and records Chromium payload source, requested/installed Playwright versions, a source timestamp with basis, and a deterministic sha256-tree-v1 digest. Existing validators/readers and provenance docs were updated; strict offline validation passes and a digest mutation fails.

title: Successful runs log browser cleanup as execution-failed-cleanup
description:
`PlaywrightRunner.executeScenario`'s `finally` block closes the runtime with the hardcoded reason
"execution-failed-cleanup" on EVERY exit path, including success
(src/runner/PlaywrightRunner.ts:282). A passing run's structured log therefore reads:

    [browser:g1] closing runtime (execution-failed-cleanup).

which actively misleads anyone reading run logs to debug a failure.

SCOPE -- READ THIS BEFORE ESTIMATING IMPACT:
This corrects MISLEADING STRUCTURED RUN-LOG TEXT ONLY. It does NOT affect shared-browser
close-reason analytics, lifecycle buckets, crash-rate backpressure, or capacity decisions.

Verified: `BrowserCloseReason` (PlaywrightRunner.ts:32) reaches exactly two places -- the log line
at PlaywrightRunner.ts:402, and `onRuntimeClosing`, whose SOLE consumer (ExecutionEngine.ts:1334)
destructures `({ generation })` and DISCARDS the reason. It is a DIFFERENT enum from
`SharedBrowserCloseReason` (SharedBrowserPool.ts:48), which is what actually feeds
runtime_browser_lifecycle_buckets and BrowserPoolEffectiveness.closeReasons via
RuntimeObservationCollector. The two enums never meet.

An earlier draft of the SRS claimed analytics contamination; tracing the consumers disproved it.
Do not reintroduce that claim.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add `execution-completed-cleanup` to the BrowserCloseReason union and use it ONLY for successful
   terminal cleanup.
2. The failure path keeps `execution-failed-cleanup`.
3. Do NOT rename existing members. `app-shutdown` and `reuse-session-swap-old-runtime` stay as-is --
   renaming churns existing log-grep habits for no behavioural gain.
4. Only add `execution-cancelled-cleanup` if it is genuinely distinguished from the existing
   `user-request`, which the cancel path already uses; otherwise reuse `user-request`.
5. Do NOT add a `browser-crash` member. `onRuntimeClosing` is documented as announcing INTENTIONAL
   teardown so the pool does not score it as a crash; a crash reason on that channel inverts the
   semantics that keep crash-rate backpressure honest.
6. Regression test asserts a successful run logs `execution-completed-cleanup` and a failed run
   logs `execution-failed-cleanup`.
7. The change note explicitly states there is NO analytics or capacity impact, and does NOT claim
   close-reason distributions will shift.
notes: Spec: docs/SRS_BROWSER_AUTOMATION_OBSERVABILITY.md FR-G1 change-dependency (Tranche 0). Low risk, but becomes load-bearing once FR-A2 puts lifecycle events on the unified timeline -- fix before the CDP work, not after.

title: Numeric record-to-replay fidelity gate for the recorder (measured %, not just pass/fail)
description:
Idea sourced from the 2026-07-22 browser-automation skills teardown
(BROWSER_AUTOMATION_SKILLS_REPORT.md sections 2A and 5). Reference implementation:
ruvnet/ruflo `browser-replay` + scripts/replay-spike.sh.

THE PATTERN WORTH STEALING: ruflo treats "is a recorded session actually replayable?" as
a MEASURED NUMBER, not a boolean. Their ADR-0001 will not move Proposed -> Accepted until
a spike demonstrates >=80% replay success across 10 distinct sites of varying DOM-drift
profiles. Per-run verdict = matched-steps / total-steps against a tolerance (default 0.85).
That converts a vague architectural bet into a ship gate.

CURRENT AWKIT STATE (verified):
- verify:recorder-flow tests recorded-actions -> flow SHAPE (Start/End nodes, wiring,
  waits as fixed-time, tab switches as Route Change). Pure logic, no browser.
- verify:recorder-locator, verify:recorder-draft, verify:flow-step-mapping cover locator
  generation, draft persistence, and round-trip serialization respectively.
- verify:runner does live checks against the mock site.
- What is MISSING: an end-to-end record -> replay loop that produces a FIDELITY
  PERCENTAGE across the mock-site scenario set. Today a replay either passes or fails a
  scenario; there is no aggregate number to watch for regression.

PROPOSED:
1. Harness that, for each applicable mock-site scenario, records a flow, replays it, and
   scores matched-steps / total-steps.
2. Emit an aggregate fidelity percentage plus a per-scenario table, so a drop is visible
   as a number rather than as one flipped assertion.
3. Pick a threshold and enforce it. ruflo chose 0.80 aggregate / 0.85 per-run; AWKIT's
   number should be set from a first baseline run, not copied.
4. Deliberately include drift-y scenarios so the metric has headroom to detect regression
   (the mock site is the Feature Test Lab - extend it per mock-site-maintainer).

WHY THIS MATTERS HERE: the randomized-test-lab round-trip work already proved that silent
fidelity loss is AWKIT's recurring failure mode (13 round-trip defects, awkit-cxa's bare
FlowStep.value drop). Those were each found by a targeted assertion after the fact. A
standing fidelity number would have shown the regression as a trend.

GOTCHAS FROM THE SOURCE MATERIAL:
- Network/timing nondeterminism produces false-fail verdicts. Pin to mock-site fixtures
  (AWKIT is offline-first, so this is easier here than upstream).
- If selector recovery needs more than one retry per step, log it - that is the signal
  the flow needs a RE-RECORD, not a replay.
- Do not let the aggregate hide a single catastrophic scenario; report both.

RELATED: awkit-wza (Randomized Automation Test Lab) - the campaign reporting phases
(awkit-wza.7) are the natural home for surfacing this number over time. Decide whether
this lands standalone or as part of that epic.
notes:
DESIGN WARNING from the v2 deep read of the reference implementation (BROWSER_AUTOMATION_SKILLS_REPORT.md section 3.3). ruflo's replay-spike.sh is the source of the >=80% gate idea AND a worked example of how to get it wrong. Three defects to avoid when building the AWKIT version:

1. Its recorded baseline is open -> snapshot -> close. No click, no fill, no navigation. There is nothing whose selector could drift, so the metric cannot observe the phenomenon it claims to measure. AWKIT's baseline scenarios MUST contain real interactions.

2. Its scoring is dead code:
     local orig_steps=2
     local replay_steps=2
     if [[ -f "$RESULTS_DIR/$label.replay.snap.json" ]] && [[ -s ... ]]; then echo PASS
   Both counters are hardcoded and never compared. The real pass condition is 'the snapshot file is non-empty'. Score matched-steps/total-steps for real, or do not publish a percentage.

3. The documented per-run tolerance (0.85) and the embedding-similarity retry are unimplemented in both the harness and the MCP tool.

Net: the gate measures 'can we open a URL twice'. Before shipping the AWKIT metric, answer explicitly: what regression turns this number red? If there is no realistic answer, the metric is decorative.
close_reason: Extended the real REC-018 Recorder journey into a measured fidelity gate across baseline, primary-locator-loss, and structural DOM drift. It derives matched/total from production log+report evidence, emits per-scenario and aggregate percentages, enforces 95% aggregate and 80% per scenario from the 100% first baseline, and persists evidence. Green baseline is 18/18=100%; removing the final stable email name produced 2/6 for that scenario and 14/18=77.78%, turning the gate red.

title: Async engine: grouped completion composition (A AND (B OR C))
description:
Completion policy is a single per-step scalar (FlowStep.completionMode) applied to ALL afterWaits, giving only flat AND (allRequired) or flat OR (anyRequired). Nested/grouped composition is not expressible.

CONCRETE GAP (found during the Electron GUI gate pre-flight, 2026-07-22): the empty-result contract

    API success AND (tableHasRows OR emptyStateVisible)

cannot be configured. resolveAnyRequired (src/runner/StepExecutor.ts) runs Promise.any across EVERY required condition INCLUDING the armed API response, so the API resolving first satisfies the whole step and neither UI outcome is ever required. That violates the rule 'a successful API status alone must not override a missing required UI outcome'. networkThenUi does not help: phase 3 requires ALL required UI outcomes (AND), so the two UI branches still cannot be OR-ed. Marking both optional means neither is required and the step passes with neither present.

NOT a regression - nothing previously worked and broke. This is missing expressiveness.

Likely shape: an explicit one-of / any-of GROUP inside afterWaits (e.g. a group condition holding N child conditions with its own required/optional flag), so allRequired can contain an OR group. Must EXTEND the existing WaitCondition union rather than fork a parallel model (see the 13 round-trip defect history), and must round-trip through toFlowStep/fromFlowStep + the JSON store.

Blocked behind: Serialization Round-Trip Hardening (extraction + executable round-trip verifier) so the new nested shape is covered by round-trip tests from day one. Also gates Electron GUI check 11 configuration 3.
notes: IMPLEMENTED (uncommitted, 2026-07-22). Extended the WaitCondition union (NOT a fork) with an anyOf OR-group: passes when ANY child passes, fails only when all fail; as one required condition under allRequired it expresses 'API success AND (tableHasRows OR emptyStateVisible)'. Runner resolves via Promise.any in executeWaitCondition (works under every completion policy); FlowValidation.clampWaits recurses; asyncCompletionReview.reviewWait rolls up worst branch. Designer: renderWaitEditor refactored to (wait,update) for recursive nested branches + '+ OR group' button + token .anyof-* CSS. verify:waits 52/0 (incl. 'API ok but neither branch -> fails'), round-trip in verify:flow-step-mapping. /async-results fixture already exposes #resultsTable + empty-state, so GUI check 11.3 is configurable; manual walkthrough remains. Close on commit + GUI 11.3 PASS.
close_reason: Closed after real-Electron GUI check 11.3 configured and persisted API AND (table rows OR empty-state text) without flattening (verify:flow-designer 58/58; screenshot captured). Runtime truth table passes rows and empty branches, rejects missing outcomes and now fails closed on an empty group (verify:waits 58/0). title: Locator recovery memory: remember the winning candidate, recover when all recorded candidates miss
description:
Idea sourced from the 2026-07-22 browser-automation skills teardown
(BROWSER_AUTOMATION_SKILLS_REPORT.md sections 2A and 5). Reference implementation:
ruvnet/ruflo AgentDB `browser-selectors` namespace, keyed <host>:<intent> ->
{selector, ref, snapshot-hash, last-success}, recovered at replay time by embedding
similarity.

CURRENT AWKIT STATE (verified in src/runner/LocatorFactory.ts resolve()):
AWKIT already does the hard part, and arguably better than the reference:
  1. container/frame context so candidates resolve inside the right subtree
  2. primary candidate, then `alternatives` in recorded order
  3. unique match wins; else the single VISIBLE match wins; else single ENABLED;
     else single IN-VIEWPORT; never guesses between equally-actionable twins
  4. all-counts-zero returns the primary so the caller's action auto-waits
  5. genuinely ambiguous -> clear diagnostic via formatFailure
Alternatives are carried on the node (recorderInitScript.buildAlternatives) rather than
looked up at replay time.

THE ACTUAL GAP - two things the recorded-alternatives design cannot do:
(a) NO RECOVERY WHEN EVERY RECORDED CANDIDATE MISSES. Once the primary and all
    alternatives resolve to zero, the step fails. There is no similarity fallback to a
    structurally-near element.
(b) NO LEARNING. Which candidate actually won last run is discarded. A flow whose primary
    has been dead for months still pays the full miss-then-fallback cost every run, and
    nothing records that the site drifted.

PROPOSED (incremental, offline - no embeddings service, no network):
1. Persist last-success per step: which candidate index resolved, plus a cheap structural
   fingerprint of the matched element. Reorder candidates by last-success on the next run.
   This is (b) alone and is low-risk.
2. Only if (1) proves insufficient: a local similarity fallback when all candidates miss -
   score visible elements against the recorded fingerprint (role/name/text/attrs/ancestry)
   and accept a match only above a high threshold, logging loudly that recovery fired.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- Offline-first: no embedding model, no remote vector store. Structural/lexical similarity
  computed locally, or nothing.
- Preserve the existing invariant from LocatorFactory: recovery may only convert
  would-be FAILURES into successes. It must never change which element an
  already-unambiguous step resolves to. Any similarity path must run strictly AFTER the
  all-candidates-missed branch.
- Never emit or match on utility/hashed classes (established recorder rule).
- Recovery firing is a signal the flow needs a re-record. Surface it, do not silently heal
  forever.

VERIFY: verify:recorder-locator for candidate ordering and fingerprinting (pure logic);
verify:runner for the live miss-then-recover path. Feeds the fidelity metric in awkit-60w.
notes: Implemented durable per-scenario/flow/step winner memory plus privacy-preserving class-free structural fingerprinting (visible text/labels/attribute values are token-hashed before persistence). Saved winner is tried first. Local recovery runs only after every recorded candidate misses and a bounded recheck, scans <=200 visible elements, requires >=0.86 score and >=0.08 unique margin, logs loudly, and tells the user to re-record. Verified: npm run verify:recorder 110/110; npm run verify:runner 89/89; mutation threshold 1.01 produced 107/110 and was reverted.

title: Instance Monitor: second read-only CDP observation client + on-disk run trace
description:
Idea sourced from the 2026-07-22 browser-automation skills teardown
(BROWSER_AUTOMATION_SKILLS_REPORT.md sections 2E and 5). Reference implementation:
Browserbase `skills/browser-trace`.

KEYSTONE FACT: every Chrome DevTools target accepts MULTIPLE concurrent CDP clients.
So an observation client can attach to a target that the runner is already driving,
enable only observation domains (Network, Console, Runtime, Log, Page), and never send
action commands. Non-intrusive by construction.

CURRENT AWKIT GAP (verified): no surface attaches a CDP client for observation.
src/session/SessionCaptureService.ts is explicitly "No CDP connection"; the
https-certificate-trust work confirmed AWKIT has only two context factories and no
CDP attach path. Instance Monitor (app/renderer/pages/InstanceMonitor.tsx,
verify:instance-monitor + verify:instance-monitor-gui) shows run state but has no
event firehose or live browser view.

PROPOSED (offline-safe, all local):
1. Observation-only CDP client attached to a running instance's Chromium. Never issues
   actions. Fails open - if attach fails the run is unaffected.
2. On-disk run trace under the existing artifacts root (NOT resources/, NOT app.asar),
   modelled on Browserbase's .o11y/<run-id>/ layout:
     manifest.json          run metadata, target, domains, started/stopped
     index.jsonl            one line per sample {ts, screenshot, dom, url}
     cdp/raw.ndjson         firehose, one JSON object per line
     cdp/summary.json       session totals + per-page domains/network/timing
     cdp/<bucket>/*.jsonl   network / console / runtime / log / page buckets
     cdp/pages/<pid>/       per-page slices, bisected on top-level Page.frameNavigated
     screenshots/<ts>.png, dom/<ts>.html
   summary.json is the analysis entry point.
3. Live browser viewing in Instance Monitor built on the same attach.

WHY IT FITS AWKIT: the layout is a filesystem tree with zero network dependency, so it
survives the offline-first constraint that rules out the cloud live_url / debugger_url
approach that browser-use and Browserbase use.

SCOPE NOTE: distinct from awkit-4km, which covers CDP diagnostics for *wait/async
resolution* (redirect chains, timing, request ids) inside the runner. This bead is the
*observability* surface: a passive tracer plus its persisted artifact plus the monitor UI.
Coordinate so both share one attach helper rather than opening two clients.

GOTCHAS FROM THE SOURCE MATERIAL:
- Do not poll screenshots/DOM faster than ~1s; 2s is the recommended default.
- Adding the DOM domain is very noisy - opt-in only.
- Always run the stop path even after a crash, or background samplers linger.
- rrweb-style DOM replay is deprecated upstream; screenshot + DOM timeline is the
  accepted visual ground truth. Do not build on rrweb.
- Retention/size policy needed: raw.ndjson grows fast. Reuse the artifacts retention
  path (verify:artifacts).

VERIFY: extend verify:instance-monitor for the trace shape and bisection, and
verify:artifacts for retention. Bisection is pure logic and can be tested without a browser.
notes: Implemented a fail-open, observation-only second CDP client with an explicit command allowlist, 2s bounded visual sampling, opt-in DOM capture, secret-redacted/capped raw NDJSON, idempotent 17-bucket and per-navigation-page bisection, durable trace artifact, and a permission-gated Instance Monitor live view. Verified: instance monitor 55/55, artifacts 23/23, real Electron GUI 18/18, runner 89/89, build PASS. Mutation: temporarily allowlisted Input.dispatchMouseEvent; focused gate failed 54/55, then reverted and passed 55/55.
close_reason: Passive CDP observation trace and live Instance Monitor view implemented and verified.
